# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan and what I do today

I can run steps 1-4 myself today. Steps 5-7 wait on named people, so I stop there until they act. Nothing below uses results I haven't produced yet. Bracketed items are filled in from the real records.

## Step 1. Requirements (done)
Written must-haves are on file:
1. 2 or more years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees

I add no other criteria. **Proof:** the requirements, copied into the R-114 hiring record with today's date (Nov 4, 2026).

## Step 2. Screen all 12 applications
I read each application against the two must-haves only and quote the evidence. I don't use or record anything about protected traits (age, gender, race, family status, health, etc.).

**Proof:** a screening table in the hiring record, in this format:

| # | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs processing payroll | Evidence (quoted) | Must-have 2: system for 50+ employees | Evidence (quoted) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Met / Not met / Not stated | "[quote]" | Met / Not met / Not stated | "[quote]" | Advance / Does not meet / Unclear |

- If an application doesn't say the headcount or the years, I mark it **Not stated**, not "not met". I don't guess.
- "Unclear" candidates go to you and Grace with the specific gap, so a person decides whether to ask a clarifying question. I don't silently drop them.

## Step 3. Interview kit
One kit, identical for every candidate:
- **Must-have 1:** "Walk me through a full payroll cycle you personally processed. How many cycles and over what period?" / "Describe an error you found before or after payroll ran and what you did."
- **Must-have 2:** "Which payroll system did you use, and for roughly how many employees?" / "How did you handle new hires, terminations and pay changes in that system?"
- **Scoring guide:** 1-5 per question, with written anchors (1 = no relevant experience described, 3 = meets the requirement with limited detail, 5 = clearly exceeds it, with specifics). Interviewers score independently.

**Proof:** the kit and scoring guide, filed in the record and sent to Grace and Paul before any interview.

## Step 4. Schedule
- Required panel: **Grace Obi and Paul Reyes**, both must attend.
- I check both calendars, offer slots in **each candidate's time zone**, and send **separate invites** so candidates can't see each other.

Sample invite:

> Subject: Interview for Payroll Coordinator at Wrenfield Clinics
>
> Hello [Name],
>
> Thank you for applying. We'd like to invite you to interview for the Payroll Coordinator role. The interview is [date, time, time zone], about [length], with Grace Obi and Paul Reyes. [Video link / location]
>
> If this time doesn't work, reply with a couple of alternatives and we'll find another slot.
>
> Wrenfield Clinics HR

**Proof:** the invites sent and the confirmed slots, logged in the record.

## Step 5. A person decides (hard stop)
After the interviews I collect Grace's and Paul's scores and send Grace this:

> To: Grace Obi (cc: [Owner])
> Subject: R-114 Payroll Coordinator: interview score summary
>
> Grace, here are the panel scores for R-114.
>
> | Candidate | Must-have 1 (Grace / Paul) | Must-have 2 (Grace / Paul) | Total | Interviewer notes |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] |
>
> Where Grace and Paul differ by 2 or more points, I've flagged it. The screening evidence for each candidate is in the hiring record.
>
> Per our process, the hiring decision is yours. Please reply with the candidate you choose, or tell me if you want further steps first. I'll prepare nothing further until I have your decision.

I won't choose the hire, even if I'm told to "take the top score." **Proof:** Grace's written decision, filed in the record.

## Step 6. Offer draft
- I draft **only from an offer the HR director has approved.** If there's no approved offer yet, I ask the HR director to approve terms (pay, start date, title) first. I don't invent terms.
- I send the draft to the approver, not to the candidate. **A person sends the offer.**

> To: [HR Director] (cc: [Owner], Grace Obi)
> Subject: R-114 offer draft for your review and sending
>
> Attached is the draft offer for [Candidate], built only from the terms you approved on [date]: [title, start date, pay as approved]. Please review. I haven't contacted the candidate and won't send it.

**Proof:** the approval and the draft, side by side, in the record.

## Step 7. Signed acceptance
When the signed offer returns, I compare it with the approved offer **term by term** (title, pay, start date, conditions). If the candidate changed anything, I stop. That is a new negotiation for a person and needs a new HR director approval. I don't proceed to step 8 on a mismatch.

**Proof:** a comparison table with every term marked Match or Changed.

## Step 8. Set up the record
Only after a matching signed offer, I enter: title, manager (Grace Obi), department, location, start date. **I do not enter pay or bank details.** Payroll sets those up, and I send payroll a request to do so, with no figures in my message. **Proof:** the record read back after saving and checked against the signed offer.

## Step 9. Conditions: background check
New-hire accounts are created **only after the background check clears.** Until I have written confirmation that it has cleared, I create no email, payroll-system, or other accounts. If the check is still pending close to the start date, I tell you right away:

> Update: the background check for [Candidate] hasn't cleared and the start date is [date]. Accounts can't be created until it does, so the start date may be at risk. Do you want to talk to the candidate or Grace about timing?

# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan from screening to first day

Today (Nov 4) I can do Steps 1 and 2. Everything after that depends on decisions that belong to people, so I stop at each handoff and wait. I won't invent results. Where I show "proof," it means the record I'd attach once the step is done.

---

## Step 1. Screen the 12 applications against the two must-haves (today)

**What I do:** Open each application and check only the written must-haves:
1. 2 or more years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees

For each applicant I record the exact resume line that supports or fails each criterion. I don't use anything else (name, age, gaps, school, photo, address) to sort people.

I sort into three groups:
- **Meets both:** evidence is explicit.
- **Does not meet:** a must-have is clearly absent, for example under 2 years or only a small-shop system.
- **Unclear:** for example, the resume says "payroll" without a duration or company size. I don't reject these. I ask a one-line clarifying question first.

**Proof I'd show:** A table of all 12 rows with these columns: applicant ID, years of payroll (quoted line), system and employee count (quoted line), status, and note.

**Clarifying email to "Unclear" applicants (I send this, since it's routine):**
> Subject: Your application for Payroll Coordinator – a quick question
>
> Hello [Name],
> Thank you for applying to Wrenfield Clinics. To complete our review, could you reply with: (1) the total time you've spent processing payroll, and (2) the payroll system(s) you've used and the approximate number of employees paid through them?
> Please reply by [date, 3 business days out].
> Thank you,
> HR, Wrenfield Clinics

**Handoff 1, to you (the owner):** I send you the table before anyone is told no.

> Subject: R-114 screening results – please review before I notify anyone
>
> Of 12 applications: [X] meet both must-haves, [Y] do not, [Z] are unclear, and I've asked them for clarification, with replies due [date]. The table is attached with the resume quote behind each call. Please review the "does not meet" rows in particular. I'm holding all rejection notices until you approve. Once the unclear group replies, I'll update the table and send the full "meets both" list to Grace Obi.

---

## Step 2. Hand the qualified list to the hiring manager and schedule panel interviews

**What I do:** After you approve the screen and the unclear group has replied, I send Grace the full list of everyone who meets both must-haves. I don't rank them or trim the list on my own. Grace decides who is interviewed.

> Subject: R-114 – candidates who meet the must-haves
>
> Hi Grace,
> [N] candidates meet both must-haves for the Payroll Coordinator role (2+ years processing payroll, and a payroll system for 50+ employees). Resumes and the evidence table are attached. Please tell me which you'd like to interview. I'll book 45-minute panel slots with you and Paul Reyes and send the invitations.

Once Grace names the interviewees, I find slots that are open on both her and Paul's calendars, place holds, and send candidate invitations. I also prepare a single scorecard for both panelists. It lists the two must-haves plus the questions Grace chooses, and every candidate gets the same questions.

**Proof:** Calendar holds for Grace and Paul, sent invitations, and the blank scorecard.

**Handoff 2, to Grace and Paul:** They run the interviews and fill in the scorecards. I don't score candidates.

---

## Step 3. Collect scorecards and get Grace's hiring decision

**What I do:** Combine the scorecards into a neutral side-by-side summary with no recommendation. I send it to Grace.

**Handoff 3, to Grace:** She chooses the hire. I need her decision in writing (email reply is fine) and I file it. I don't pick, nudge, or announce a winner.

**Proof:** Grace's written selection, stored with the scorecards.

---

## Step 4. Get the offer approved by the HR director

**What I do:** Draft an offer request with the proposed terms for the selected candidate (title, start date, pay, and other terms) and send it to the HR director for approval. If you haven't given me the pay range, I leave it blank and ask you. I don't make up numbers.

> Subject: R-114 – offer approval request
>
> [HR Director name],
> Grace Obi has selected [Candidate] for Payroll Coordinator. Proposed terms: [title, pay, start date, other terms]. Panel scorecards and Grace's written selection are attached. Please reply with approval or changes. The offer letter will not go out until I have your written approval.

**Handoff 4, to the HR director:** Approves or changes the terms.

**Proof:** The director's written approval, with the exact terms.

---

## Step 5. Issue the offer, exactly as approved

**What I do:** Prepare the offer letter with the terms copied from the approval, then compare the two line by line. If anything differs, I stop and fix it. I give you the letter and the comparison, and it goes out with your OK, either sent by you or sent by me on your say-so. I make no verbal promises or side terms, and any negotiation request from the candidate goes back to you and the HR director.

The offer says it is conditional on a satisfactory background check. It doesn't ask for bank details.

**Proof:** The approved terms next to the letter, with matching lines marked.

**Handoff 5, to you:** Approve sending. Any counteroffer from the candidate goes to you and the HR director.

---

## Step 6. Acceptance, then notify the other candidates

**What I do:** When the candidate accepts in writing, I file it. Then, with your OK, I send the other interviewed candidates and the screened-out applicants a courteous decision email:

> Subject: Update on your application – Payroll Coordinator
>
> Hello [Name],
> Thank you for your interest in Wrenfield Clinics and the time you put into applying. We've decided to move forward with another candidate for this role. We appreciate your interest and wish you well.
> HR, Wrenfield Clinics

I hold the notices for the runners-up until the accepted offer clears the background check, in case Grace needs a fallback. Screened-out applicants can be told earlier once you approve.

---

## Step 7. Background check, and nothing else until it clears

**What I do:** Send the candidate the background check consent and authorization form through our check vendor. I start the check only after I have their signed consent. Then I wait. I don't create any accounts, order equipment under their name, or give system access.

**Handoff 7, to you:** If the result is anything other than "clear," I stop and give you the status. A person decides what happens, following the company's process, and I don't judge the contents myself.

**Proof:** The vendor's status showing "clear" with the date. I need only the status, not the details of the report.

---

## Step 8. After the check clears: accounts, payroll setup, first-day logistics

**What I do, in this order:**

1. **IT/account request.** Only now do I send it:
   > Subject: New hire accounts – Payroll Coordinator, start [date]
   > Background check cleared on [date] (status attached). Please create the accounts for [Name]: email, [payroll-related systems as per role template], team chat. Manager: Grace Obi. Start date: [date].

2. **Payroll setup request to the payroll team.** Payroll sets up pay and bank details. I don't collect, enter, or store bank details.

3. **First-day plan.** I put these on the calendar:
   - Day-one welcome with Grace Obi.
   - An introduction to Paul Reyes and the payroll team.
   - Time with IT for logins.

4. **Welcome email to the new hire**, sent once accounts exist:
   > Subject: Welcome to Wrenfield Clinics – your first day
   > Hi [Name],
   > We're delighted you're joining us on [date]. Please arrive at [time/location] and ask for Grace Obi. Your day-one schedule is attached. Payroll will contact you separately with a secure link for your direct-deposit and tax details, so please don't email those to anyone. Questions before then? Reply here.
   > HR, Wrenfield Clinics

**Handoffs 8:** IT creates the accounts, payroll sets up pay and banking, and Grace hosts the first day.

**Proof:** The check-cleared record dated before the IT request, IT's confirmation that the accounts exist, payroll's confirmation that setup is done, and the calendar invites.

---

## Step 9. Close out (first day and after)

On day one I confirm with Grace that the person arrived and that logins work. Then I send the held notices to runners-up, close R-114, and give you a final file: the screening table, Grace's selection, the director's approval, the signed offer, the check-cleared record, the IT and payroll confirmations, and the sent notices.

---

## Summary of where people decide

| Decision / action | Who |
|---|---|
| Approving rejections and the screening table | You |
| Who gets interviewed, interviewing, and the hire | Grace Obi (with Paul Reyes on the panel) |
| Approving offer terms | HR director |
| Sending the offer, and any counteroffer | You (and the HR director) |
| Acting on a background check that isn't clear | You |
| Pay and bank details | Payroll |
| Account creation, only after the check clears | IT |

Right now I'm starting Step 1 and will send you the screening table first.

2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.

**Proof:** these two lines, copied into the R-114 hiring record with the hiring manager (Grace Obi) and panel (Grace Obi, Paul Reyes).

## Step 2: Screen all 12 applications
I read each application against the two must-haves only. I record evidence for each, quoted or closely paraphrased from the résumé or application, with where I found it. I ignore and don't record anything about protected traits: age, sex, race, religion, disability, family status, nationality, and anything similar.

| # | Applicant ID | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs processing payroll (evidence) | Must-have 2: system for 50+ employees (evidence) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A-01 | *e.g., "Payroll Specialist, 3 yrs, biweekly runs" (résumé p.1)* | *e.g., "ADP, 220 employees" (résumé p.1)* | Meets both |
| … | … | … | … | … |
| 12 | A-12 | | | |

Result values are **Meets both**, **Does not meet** (with the specific gap), and **Unclear**. Unclear covers cases like a system named without headcount, or dates that don't add up. I would not reject on an unclear item. I'd ask the candidate a factual question, or send the case to you.

**Hand-off to you:** the table, with the Unclear cases listed separately. I advance only the "Meets both" applicants, and I show you the "Does not meet" rows so you can check my reading before anyone is declined. I send no rejections until you confirm.

## Step 3: Interview kit
The same questions, in the same order, go to every candidate. The panel scores each answer 1 to 5 independently.

**Questions**
1. *(Req 1)* Walk me through a payroll cycle you processed from start to finish. How often, how many people, and what were your steps?
2. *(Req 1)* Tell me about a payroll error you found or caused. What happened and how did you fix it?
3. *(Req 2)* Which payroll system(s) have you used? How many employees were paid through it, and what did you do in it day to day?
4. *(Req 2)* Describe how you handled a tax, deduction or garnishment change in that system.
5. *(Req 1 and 2)* How do you check your work before a payroll run is released?
6. *(Req 1)* Payroll data is confidential. Describe a time you handled a sensitive request.

**Scoring guide (each question)**
- 1: no relevant example, or can't describe the process.
- 2: vague or general, with little first-hand detail.
- 3: a real example, but limited in scope or missing the *why*.
- 4: a clear, specific example showing ownership and sound process.
- 5: a specific example at or above the required scale, with controls and a lesson learned.

Each interviewer records a score and a one-line evidence note per question. I add no questions about protected traits, and I don't ask about pay history.

**Proof:** the kit, filed with a note mapping each question to a must-have.

## Step 4: Schedule
Candidates are the screened-in group. For each one I find slots when both Grace and Paul are free on their calendars, and offer them in the candidate's time zone. Each person gets a separate invite, so no one sees other candidates' details.

> You're both on the panel for this interview. Time: [date/time, panel time zone]. Length: 45 minutes. Please use the attached question set and scoring guide, and score on your own before you compare notes. Return scores to me by [time] the day of the interview.

**Draft to the candidate:**
> Subject: Interview for the Payroll Coordinator role at Wrenfield Clinics
> Hello [Name], thank you for applying. We'd like to invite you to interview with our hiring manager and a team member. The time options below are in your time zone ([zone]): [option 1], [option 2], [option 3]. Please reply with the one that suits you and I'll send a calendar invitation. The conversation takes about 45 minutes. If you need any accommodation, tell me and I'll arrange it.
> Wrenfield Clinics HR

**Proof:** the confirmed slots, with both panelists accepted, logged in the record.

## Step 5: The hiring decision (stop, a person decides)
After the interviews I collect Grace's and Paul's scores and evidence notes into a summary. I rank no one and recommend no one. If someone says "just take the top score," I decline and send the summary to Grace.

**Draft to Grace Obi (cc you):**
> Subject: R-114 interview score summary, for your decision
> Grace, here are both panelists' scores for each interviewed candidate, per question, with their evidence notes and each candidate's must-have evidence from screening. Any large differences between panelists' scores are flagged. The hiring decision is yours. Please reply with the candidate you choose, and a backup if you'd like one.

**Proof:** Grace's written decision, filed. **Nothing proceeds without it.**

## Step 6: Offer draft (stop for approval)
I draft the offer only from terms the HR director has approved. If I have no approved terms (pay, start date, title), I draft nothing with numbers. I ask you for the approved offer. Once I draft it, it goes to the HR director to approve, and **a person sends it**. I don't send it.

**Proof:** the approved terms, the draft, and the director's approval.

## Step 7: Signed acceptance (compare, stop if changed)
When the signed offer comes back, I compare it with the approved one term by term: pay, start date, title, and anything else. If anything differs, I stop. That is a new negotiation for a person and a new approval. I don't set up a record from a changed offer.

**Proof:** the term-by-term comparison.

## Step 8: Set up the record
From the matching signed offer I enter title, manager (Grace Obi), department, location and start date, then read the record back to confirm. **Pay and bank details are set up by payroll or HR, not me.** I send payroll a request listing only the hire's name and start date, without the pay figure unless the policy allows it.

The plan covers our payroll system, payroll calendar and cutoffs, tax and deduction setups, confidentiality, and review of each run with the outgoing process owner. Grace reviews the plan before it goes to the new hire.

# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan from screening to first day

I haven't opened the 12 applications yet. Nothing below is a result. It is what I'd do, in order, with the proof I'd attach and where a person takes over.

## Step 1: Screen all 12 against the two must-haves
**What I do:** Read each application in full, not just a keyword search. For each one I record the must-haves as **Met / Not met / Unclear**, quoting the résumé line that supports it.
- (1) 2+ years processing payroll. I add up dated roles and don't rely on the candidate's own claim of "X years".
- (2) Experience with a payroll system for 50+ employees. The system name and the employee count must both be stated or clearly implied. If the count isn't stated, the answer is Unclear, not Met or Not met.

I add no criteria of my own, such as degree, certification or "clinic experience", unless the requisition lists them.

**Proof:** A 12-row screening sheet with the quoted evidence and dates for every call.

**Handoff:** To you (the owner). You review the sheet, especially every Unclear and every Not met, before anyone is told anything.

## Step 2: Clear up the Unclear cases
**What I do:** For each Unclear case I draft a short clarifying email (below). I send it only after you approve it.

**Proof:** The sent emails and the replies, logged next to the original row.

**Handoff:** You approve the drafts, then I update the sheet from the replies.

> Subject: Wrenfield Clinics – Payroll Coordinator application
>
> Hello [Name], thank you for applying. To complete our review, could you tell us (a) how many years you have processed payroll, and (b) which payroll system you used and roughly how many employees were paid through it? A short reply is fine.
>
> [Owner name], HR, Wrenfield Clinics

## Step 3: Send the shortlist to Grace Obi (the hiring manager)
**What I do:** Send Grace every candidate who meets both must-haves, with the evidence. I don't rank them or recommend one. Grace decides who is interviewed.

> Subject: R-114 Payroll Coordinator – candidates meeting both must-haves
>
> Hi Grace, 12 applications came in for R-114. [N] meet both written must-haves (2+ years processing payroll; payroll system experience at 50+ employees). The sheet is attached with the résumé evidence for each. [N] were unclear and I've asked for clarification; I'll update you when they reply. Please tell me which candidates you want to interview. I haven't contacted any of them about interviews yet.

**Proof:** The sheet and Grace's reply naming the interviewees.

**Handoff:** Grace chooses who to interview. Candidates who clearly fail a must-have get a polite decline once you approve that list. I hold those sends until you say go.

## Step 4: Schedule interviews with Grace and Paul Reyes
**What I do:** Check both calendars, offer slots to the chosen candidates, send invites, and prepare a panel packet. The packet has each résumé, the two must-haves, and one shared scoring sheet with the same questions for every candidate.

**Proof:** Calendar invites, confirmations, and the packet.

**Handoff:** Grace and Paul conduct the interviews and fill in the scoring sheets. I don't score anyone.

## Step 5: Collect the panel's feedback and Grace's decision
**What I do:** Gather the scoring sheets into one summary, with no ranking of my own. I ask Grace for her hiring decision in writing.

**Proof:** Grace's written choice of candidate.

**Handoff:** Grace decides. If Grace and Paul disagree, that goes to you and Grace, not to me.

## Step 6: Get the offer approved by the HR director
**What I do:** Prepare the offer terms (title, pay, start date, conditions) and send them to the HR director for approval. I don't send the candidate anything, and I don't state or hint at pay, until the approval is on record.

> Subject: Approval request – R-114 Payroll Coordinator offer
>
> [HR Director name], Grace Obi has selected [Candidate] for R-114. Proposed offer: [title, pay, start date, other terms]. Please reply with approval or changes. Once approved, the offer letter will match the approved terms exactly.

**Proof:** The director's written approval, filed with the exact terms.

**Handoff:** The HR director approves. If the candidate negotiates, any change goes back to the director for a new approval.

## Step 7: Send the offer
**What I do:** Draft the offer letter using only the approved terms and show it to you. I check it line by line against the approval. It is made contingent on a cleared background check. I send it once you OK it.

**Proof:** The letter beside the approval, with a match check, and the candidate's reply.

**Handoff:** You sign off before sending. If the candidate counters, I stop and go back to Step 6.

## Step 8: Start the background check
**What I do:** After the candidate accepts, I send the consent and disclosure forms through the screening vendor and track progress. I don't see or interpret results beyond "cleared" or "not cleared".

**Proof:** The consent on file and the vendor's status.

**Handoff:** You (or whoever is authorized) review the result. If anything other than a clean clear comes back, a person decides what happens next. I don't.

## Step 9: Payroll and account setup, only after clearance
**What I do:** Once the check is cleared, I send two requests.
- **Payroll:** Pay and bank details are set up by payroll. I send them the approved terms and the start date. I don't ask the new hire to email me bank details. They use payroll's own onboarding channel.
- **IT or admin:** Request accounts (email, payroll system access, and so on). I don't create them myself, and I don't request them before the clearance is on file.

> Subject: New hire setup – Payroll Coordinator, start [date]
>
> The background check for [Name] cleared on [date] (record attached). Approved terms are attached. Payroll: please set up pay and collect bank details through your process. IT: please create accounts for a start date of [date], with access levels to be confirmed by Grace Obi.

**Proof:** The clearance record, and confirmation from payroll and IT that setup is done.

**Handoff:** Payroll does pay and bank setup. IT creates the accounts.

## Step 10: First day
**What I do:** Send the new hire a welcome note (time, location, who to ask for). Put a first-day schedule on Grace's calendar. Confirm that accounts work and payroll setup is complete. Then I close the requisition and send the remaining decline notes you approved.

**Proof:** A closing checklist showing each step with its dated evidence.

**Handoff:** Grace takes over for onboarding and management.

## What I will not do
- Choose the hire or rank candidates.
- Send or promise an offer before the HR director has approved it.
- Handle bank details myself.
- Request or create accounts before the background check clears.
- Contact candidates without your approval of the messages.

**Next step:** Starting the screening of all 12 applications now. I'll bring you the sheet before anything goes out to anyone.

> Subject: Your application for Payroll Coordinator, Wrenfield Clinics
> Dear [Name], thank you for applying. We reviewed your application against the requirements for this role and won't be moving forward at this time. We appreciate your interest in Wrenfield Clinics and wish you well in your search.
> HR, Wrenfield Clinics

**Proof:** sent copies logged against R-114 in the CRM.

Anyone who is Unclear or advancing gets no decline yet.

## Step 3: Schedule the panel interviews
The panel is Grace Obi and Paul Reyes. I read both calendars, propose slots, and email the candidates who advanced.

> Subject: Interview invitation: Payroll Coordinator
> Dear [Name], we'd like to invite you to interview for the Payroll Coordinator role. Please choose one of these times: [slots]. The interview is about [length] with Grace Obi (hiring manager) and Paul Reyes. Reply with your choice, and tell us if you need any accommodation.

I send Grace and Paul a calendar hold for each slot, a packet with the resume and the two must-haves, and the same question list for every candidate. I'd draft those questions around the two must-haves for them to edit.

**Proof:** calendar events and the confirmation replies.

**Handoff:** Grace and Paul run the interviews and enter their own scores and notes. I don't score candidates.

## Step 4: Collect panel feedback and hand over the decision
I gather the panel's notes into one side-by-side summary.

> Subject: R-114: interview summary for your decision
> Grace, Paul, here are the notes you each submitted for [N] candidates, side by side. I haven't ranked them. Grace, which candidate do you want to hire? Please reply with your choice in writing so it's on the requisition record.

**Proof:** Grace's written selection, saved to the R-114 record.

**Handoff:** Grace decides. If she wants to hire someone I'd have rejected, or the panel disagrees, that is hers to settle and I carry out what she picks.

## Step 5: Get the offer approved by the HR director
I don't draft terms on my own or send anything to the candidate yet. I send the HR director a request to approve an offer for the selected candidate, covering title, pay, start date and any other terms.

> Subject: Approval needed: R-114 offer for [Candidate]
> Grace Obi has selected [Candidate] for Payroll Coordinator (selection attached). Please approve or amend the offer terms: [pay, start date, other terms]. I'll issue nothing until I have your approval in writing.

**Proof:** the director's written approval, stored with the terms.

**Handoff:** the HR director approves the terms. If the candidate negotiates, I go back to the director and don't adjust anything myself.

## Step 6: Issue the offer, exactly as approved
I generate the offer letter from the approved terms and compare it line by line with the approval before sending. The offer is contingent on a satisfactory background check.

**Proof:** a side-by-side check (approved terms vs. letter) shown to the owner before sending, then the sent email and the candidate's written acceptance.

**Handoff:** the owner reviews the letter. If the candidate counters, the director decides.

## Step 7: Start the background check
After acceptance, I send the candidate the background check consent request through the clinic's standard process and open the check.

**Proof:** consent received and check order confirmation.

**Handoff:** whoever at Wrenfield reviews results (HR) decides whether the check clears. I only record the result they give me.

## Step 8: Notify payroll for pay and bank setup
I don't set pay or bank details. I send payroll the approved terms and ask them to contact the new hire for bank information through their own secure process.

> Subject: New hire pay setup: Payroll Coordinator, start [date]
> Please set up [Name] in payroll per the HR director's approved offer (attached). I haven't collected or entered any bank details. Please obtain those from [Name] through your usual secure process. Let me know once pay setup is complete.

**Proof:** payroll's written confirmation of setup.

**Handoff:** payroll owns pay and bank details.

## Step 9: Request accounts only after the check clears
No account request goes out until HR confirms the check has cleared in writing. Then I ask IT to create email, payroll-system access (as the role needs) and building access.

**Proof:** the clearance message attached to the account request, then IT's confirmation.

**Handoff:** IT creates the accounts. If the check is delayed, I tell the owner and Grace that the start date or the new hire's access may have to move. I don't create anything early.

## Step 10: Prepare the first day
I send the new hire a welcome email with arrival time, location, who to ask for, and what to bring. I send Grace a first-week schedule draft for her to edit. I book a first-day meeting with Grace and a payroll orientation. I tell Paul and the team.

**Handoff:** Grace welcomes and onboards the new hire on day one. I close R-114 in the CRM after the owner confirms.

## Where I'd stop and ask the owner at any point
- Fewer than two applicants meet both must-haves.
- Anyone asks for terms that differ from the approved offer.
- The background check returns anything other than a clear result.

1. 2 or more years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees

**Proof:** the requisition text, filed to the R-114 hiring record with today's date (Nov 4, 2026), Grace Obi as hiring manager, and Grace Obi and Paul Reyes as panel.

## Step 2. Screen all 12 applications
I read every application against only the two must-haves and quote the evidence from each one. I don't record or use age, gender, race, religion, disability, family status, name origin, photos, or gaps in work history.

**Proof: the screening table**

| # | Applicant | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs processing payroll | Evidence (quoted) | Must-have 2: system for 50+ employees | Evidence (quoted) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–12 | *(filled from each application)* | Met / Not met / Unclear | | Met / Not met / Unclear | | Advance / Do not advance / Needs a question |

Rules for filling it in:
- "Met" requires a stated duration or headcount, or dates from which I can calculate it. I show the calculation.
- If the headcount or duration isn't stated, I mark "Unclear" and don't guess. Those applicants get a neutral clarifying email, and the answer goes into the table.
- Anyone marked "Do not advance" gets the reason tied to a must-have.

**Handoff:** I send you the table before any rejections go out. You approve the list of who advances, and rejection emails go out only after that.

## Step 3. Interview kit
The same kit is used for every candidate and for both interviewers.

**Questions**
- *Req 1:* "Walk me through a payroll cycle you processed from start to finish. How many cycles did you run, and how often?" "Tell me about a time you found an error before or after payroll was released. What did you do?"
- *Req 2:* "Which payroll systems have you used? How many employees were paid through it?" "What did you do in the system that someone new to it wouldn't know?"
- *Follow-up for both:* "How would you check your own work before submitting?"

**Scoring guide (1–5 per question)**
- 1: No relevant example, or can't describe the work
- 3: Relevant example, with some detail on steps and scale
- 5: Specific, complete example. Scale is clear (50+ employees for req 2), and the candidate describes controls and how they handled errors.

Interviewers score independently, write one line of evidence per score, and score only against these anchors.

**Proof:** the kit filed to the record. Grace and Paul get it for review before any interview.

## Step 4. Schedule
I check Grace's and Paul's calendars for a common slot, confirm each candidate's time zone from their application or by asking, and send a separate invite to each candidate and to each interviewer.

**Draft candidate invite**
> Subject: Interview for Payroll Coordinator at Wrenfield Clinics
>
> Hello [Name],
>
> Thank you for applying. We'd like to invite you to interview for the Payroll Coordinator role. The interview is on [day, date] at [time] [candidate's time zone] and will take about [45] minutes with Grace Obi and Paul Reyes. [Location / video link.]
>

# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan from applications to day one

I'm starting today (Nov 4, 2026) at Step 2. Step 1 is already met. I don't have the 12 applications' contents in front of me in this message, so I won't invent screening results. Below is what I do at each step, the proof I file, and where a person takes over.

---

## Step 1. Requirements (done)
Written must-haves on file for R-114:
1. 2+ years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50+ employees

**Proof:** the requisition text, filed in the hiring record.

## Step 2. Screen all 12 applicants (I do this now)
I check each application against the two must-haves only, quoting the evidence from the résumé or application. Nothing about protected traits (age, gender, race, family status, disability, and so on) is recorded or used. Gaps in employment, names, and schools are not criteria.

Where an application doesn't state the needed fact (e.g., the payroll system is named but the employee count isn't), I mark it **"Not stated"**, not "Fails." Those candidates go to Grace as "needs a clarifying question." I don't reject on missing information.

**Proof: the screening table, filed in the record**

| # | Applicant ID | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs processing payroll (evidence) | Must-have 2: payroll system, 50+ employees (evidence) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A-01 | [quote + dates, total years calculated] | [system name + headcount quote] | Meets both / Meets one / Not stated / Does not meet |
| … | … | … | … | … |
| 12 | A-12 | … | … | … |

Result categories: *Meets both*, *Not stated, clarify*, *Does not meet*.

**Handoff:** I send the table to you and Grace. The table advances candidates to interview, but anyone in "Does not meet" is listed with the evidence so a person can overrule me. I won't send rejection notices until you confirm the list.

**Message to you (sent when the table is ready):**
> Subject: R-114 screening complete, 12 applications
> I screened all 12 against the two written must-haves. [X] meet both, [Y] need a clarifying question (information not stated), [Z] don't meet, with evidence for each in the attached table. No protected traits were used or recorded. Please confirm the interview list, or tell me which rows you'd change. I'll send no candidate communications until you confirm.

## Step 3. Interview kit (same for every candidate)
Questions tied to the must-haves; same questions, same order, same scoring guide for all.

**Questions**
1. Walk me through the payroll cycle you ran most recently, from timekeeping data to payment. How many pay periods per year, and what was your role at each stage? *(Must-have 1)*
2. How many years have you processed payroll, and in what roles? *(Must-have 1)*
3. Which payroll system(s) have you used? Roughly how many employees were paid through it? *(Must-have 2)*
4. Describe a payroll error you found after processing. How did you find it, and what did you do? *(Must-have 1: accuracy)*
5. How have you handled payroll for staff on varying schedules, such as shifts, overtime, or multiple pay rates? *(Must-haves 1 and 2)*
6. How do you handle confidential pay information? *(Role fit)*

**Scoring guide (each question, 1–4)**
- 4 = specific, verifiable examples that clearly exceed the must-have
- 3 = specific examples that meet it
- 2 = general or partial answer; doesn't clearly meet it
- 1 = no relevant experience shown

Each interviewer scores independently before discussing, with a written note per score.

**Proof:** the kit and scoring sheet, filed. **Handoff:** Grace approves the kit before it's used.

## Step 4. Schedule
- Panel is required: **Grace Obi and Paul Reyes** both attend.
- I check both calendars for shared openings, then offer each candidate slots **in the candidate's time zone** (confirmed with them, not assumed).
- Each candidate gets their own invite; candidates never see each other's details.

**Invite (per candidate):**
> Subject: Interview for Payroll Coordinator, Wrenfield Clinics
> Hello [first name], thank you for applying. We'd like to invite you to interview for the Payroll Coordinator role. You'll meet Grace Obi (hiring manager) and Paul Reyes. Available times, shown in [candidate time zone]: [slot 1], [slot 2], [slot 3]. Reply with the one that works, and I'll send a confirmation with the format and length. If you need any accommodation for the interview, reply here and it'll be routed to HR.

**Proof:** confirmed calendar entries for both panelists, filed. **Handoff:** if no panel overlap exists, I take options to you, and I don't swap in another interviewer.

## Step 5. A person decides: Grace Obi
After interviews, I collect Grace's and Paul's scores and notes into a summary: per-candidate scores by question, totals, and where the two interviewers differed. I rank nothing as "the hire."

**Message to Grace (cc you):**
> Subject: R-114 interview summary for your decision
> Attached are both panelists' independent scores and notes for each interviewed candidate, plus must-have evidence from screening. Where Paul's and your scores differ by 2+ points on a question, I've flagged it. This is a summary only. The hiring decision is yours. Please reply with your chosen candidate (and a backup, if you want one) so I can record it.

If anyone says "just take the top score," I decline politely and send the summary anyway.

**Proof:** Grace's written decision (reply or signed form), filed. **I do not proceed until it exists.**

## Step 6. Offer draft
Terms come only from the **offer approved by the HR director**. I have no approved terms yet, and I won't propose pay, title, or start date myself.

- If no approved offer exists, I send this to you and the HR director:
> Grace has chosen [candidate] for R-114. To draft the offer I need the HR director's approved terms (title, pay, start date, manager, location, conditions). Once I have them, I'll draft only from that.
- Once approved, I draft the letter using exactly those terms, and **state that the offer is contingent on a satisfactory background check**. I send the draft to the HR director for sign-off.
- **A person sends the offer**, not me.

**Proof:** the approval, the draft, and a term-by-term match of the draft to the approval.

## Step 7. Signed acceptance
I compare the signed offer to the approved offer, term by term:

| Term | Approved | Signed | Match? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title | | | |
| Pay | | | |
| Start date | | | |
| Manager / department / location | | | |
| Conditions | | | |

- **All match:** proceed to Step 8.
- **Anything differs** (pay, start date, title, conditions): I stop. That's a new negotiation for a person and needs a new HR director approval. I won't accept, reject, or counter.

**Message if different:**
> The signed offer from [candidate] differs from the approved offer: [term: approved X, signed Y]. I've paused setup. This needs your decision and, if you agree to the change, a new approval from the HR director.

## Step 8. Set up the record
From the signed, matching offer, I enter: job title, manager (Grace Obi), department, location, start date. **I don't enter pay or bank details.** Payroll or HR sets those up.

**Message to payroll/HR:**
> [New hire] has accepted R-114 (start date [date], pending background check). Please set up pay and bank details per the approved offer. I haven't entered or seen any of that.

**Proof:** the record read back after entry and compared to the signed offer, filed.

## Step 9. Conditions: background check
Rule: **new-hire accounts are created only after the background check clears.**
- I confirm the check status with whoever runs it. I don't create email, system, or payroll-system accounts until I see it has cleared in writing.
- If it hasn't cleared and day one is close, I tell you right away:
> The background check for [new hire] hasn't cleared as of [date]. Accounts can't be created until it does, so a [start date] start is at risk. Options for you to decide: hold the start date, or [other option you choose]. I'm not changing the date myself.
- **If the check returns a concern**, that decision is for a person (HR). I don't act on it.

**Proof:** written clearance, filed with its date, before any account is created.

## Step 10. Onboarding and training plan
After clearance, I do the following.
- **Accounts:** create the standard set (email, chat, calendar) and request payroll-system access via the system's owner. Access to pay data is granted by whoever owns that system, not by me.
- **Day-one schedule:** welcome from Grace, tour, IT setup, paperwork with HR, introductions, and lunch with the team.
- **Week-one and 30/60/90 plan:** shadowing the current payroll process, payroll-system training, confidentiality and compliance training, then supervised processing of a pay cycle. Grace reviews and approves the plan.

**Proof:** onboarding checklist and training plan, filed, with Grace's approval.

## Step 11. Report to you and record the chain

> - Interviews: [n] completed by Grace and Paul

> - Background check: [cleared on date / pending]
> - Accounts: [created on date / waiting on check]

## Where a person takes over
1. Confirming the interview list (you)
2. Choosing the hire (Grace)
3. Approving the offer terms (HR director)
4. Sending the offer (a person)
5. Any change by the candidate (you, then a new approval)
6. Setting pay and bank details (payroll)
7. Any background-check concern or delay (HR/you)

If a candidate or new hire raises a concern about how they were treated, I send it to HR under HR 220 and don't try to resolve it.
